story.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
paras: The Flames (6-7-0) beat Seattle 6-2 on Friday, and the Sharks (7-6-1) beat Vancouver 3-2 on Thursday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames fifth (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 16th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Flames’ record (.462) is about what their chances are worth. The Sharks’ record (.536) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.386), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Flames (3rd lowest) and the Sharks (4th lowest) both do a lot of their shooting from distance. The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). On the other side, the Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks, and they have the edge over the Sharks on preventing dangerous shots.

Joel Farabee (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (5 G / 5 A / 10 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals, with seven points in his last five games. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Dustin Wolf (2-4-0 / .848 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start. Yaroslav Askarov (4-5-0 / .900 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for San Jose.
